newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soymeal ends limit down on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soymeal ends limit down on fund sales.

text.p: Heavy fund selling pushed May and July soymeal futures down the $10.00 per ton trading limit where they stayed until the close and soyoil futures also ended lower, traders said.
"The funds were really hitting the meal," said one floor trader. "This whole thing is a mess."
Commodity funds were estimated to have sold at least 4,000 lots of soymeal on the day, traders said.
Limit-down losses in nearby soybean futures caused moderate to heavy weakness in soyoil futures, floor traders said.
However, activity in that pit was not as heavy as it was in soybeans or soymeal, traders said.
Talk that China was re-selling U.S. soymeal in world export markets also pressured the market, floor traders said.
Reports of soybean exports from Brazil to the U.S. spurred concerns about soymeal shipments from South America to the U.S., traders said.

CBOT soymeal ended down 0.50 to $10.00 per ton lower with May down $10.00 at $281.50 and July down $10.00 at $278.90. Soyoil futures ended down 0.10 to 0.17 cent per lb with May down 0.17 at 23.87 cents.
